title: @Transactional and self-calls
context: A @Service has a method a() that calls this.b(). b() is annotated @Transactional(propagation = Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW). Does b() run in its own new transaction? Explain why, and how you would fix it.
answer: No. Spring implements @Transactional with a proxy around the bean. Only calls that come in through the proxy get transaction handling; a() calling b() on `this` goes straight to the target object, so the annotation on b() is ignored and b() simply joins whatever transaction a() is in (or none). To fix it, move b() to a separate bean and inject it, use TransactionTemplate to start the new transaction programmatically, or (rarely) switch to AspectJ weaving, which works on self-calls.

points.title: No, it doesn't get a new transaction
points.why: The REQUIRES_NEW setting on b() never takes effect for a self-call.

points.title: Transactions are applied by a proxy
points.why: Spring wraps the bean in a proxy (JDK dynamic proxy or CGLIB) that starts and commits transactions around calls.

points.title: Self-invocation bypasses the proxy
points.why: this.b() calls the target object directly, so the proxy never sees the call.

points.title: Fix: separate bean or programmatic transaction
points.why: Calling through another bean goes through its proxy; TransactionTemplate makes the boundary explicit.

points.title: AspectJ weaving works on self-calls
points.why: Compile- or load-time weaving changes the class itself, so there is no proxy to bypass.
